conventions.convention: The finite graph has nonempty finite vertex set X, finite directed edge set E, and positive spin dimension r. A link from x to y transforms by exp(i(θ_x−θ_y)); its hopping block occupies matrix position (x,y). Vertex phases are independent external parameters.

Formal series use coefficientwise addition and Cauchy multiplication over C[[z]], without numerical convergence. K0 is invertible, and both K0 and V transform by conjugation with the vertex-phase matrix.

Grassmann bars name independent generators. The ordered top monomial is barψ1⋯barψd ψ1⋯ψd, and integration is its coefficient multiplied by (−1)^(d(d+1)/2). Coefficients belong to a commutative unital complex algebra.

The photon one-particle measure is d³k, the pairing is linear in its second variable, and transversality means k·f(k)=0 almost everywhere. Countable Choice is assumed. The energy multiplier is ℏc|k| on its maximal square-integrability domain, with k in inverse metres.

The geometric metric is η=(−+++), while the slash contraction uses h=−η=(+---). Γ(p)=γ⁰p⁰−Σγʲp_j, the Dirac adjoint is u†β, and the tree lemma requires μ>0. Rational propagators are used only when h(p,p)−μ² is nonzero.

The coherent cutoff satisfies 0<ε<κ with fixed κ>0. Its angular profile is transverse and square-integrable, with strictly positive squared integral C_b. Coherent vectors are exp(−||f||²/2) times the exponential vector, including the vacuum sector n=0.

Longitudinal decoupling applies to the explicitly specified on-shell currents and a coefficient c(k) finite at the chosen momentum. It does not authorize singular distribution products or arbitrary diagrammatic gauge-independence claims.

load_bearing.statement: For the finite formal matrices K=K0+zV and S of def-qft-qed-formal-ring, with d≥1, invertible K0 and covariant coefficient matrices, S is a two-sided inverse of K and transforms coefficientwise as S(z;ζ^θ)=Dθ S(z;ζ)Dθ⁻¹. Along the specified phase path, δK=i[Θ,K] and δS=i[Θ,S]=−S(δK)S. For finite invertible A,B, B⁻¹(B−A)A⁻¹=A⁻¹−B⁻¹.

For fixed κ>0 and transverse b∈L²(S²;C³) with C_b=∫|b|²dΩ>0, the specified cutoff family satisfies ||fε||²=C_b log(κ/ε) and ⟨C(fε),H_ph C(fε)⟩=ℏc C_b(κ−ε). Each C(fε) is a unit vector in D(H_ph). As ε decreases to zero, C(fε) converges weakly to zero and has no strong Fock-space limit.

For μ>0 and p,p+k with nonzero off-shell denominators, S0(p+k)Γ(k)S0(p)=S0(p)−S0(p+k); finite chains telescope with both endpoint terms retained. Future-shell spinors satisfying the stated Dirac equations obey bar u(p′)Γ(p−p′)u(p)=0 and bar v(q)Γ(p+q)u(p)=0.
For admissible covariant finite graph families with invertible K0, define K(z;ζ)=K0(ζ)+zV(ζ) and S(z;ζ)=Σ(n≥0)(−zK0(ζ)⁻¹V(ζ))ⁿK0(ζ)⁻¹ over C[[z]]. Define determinant by the finite Leibniz formula.

For the stated equal-mass future-shell Dirac currents with k=p1−p1′=p2′−p2 and finite c(k), a longitudinal kernel change ΔDμν=c(k)kμkν contracts to zero. Pure-gauge polarization shifts leave contractions with the conserved tree-current forms of lem-qft-qed-tree-ward unchanged.

For d≥1 and K∈M_d(C[[z]]), the normalized top-coefficient integral of exp(−Σ barψ_i K_ij ψ_j) equals det K. If K′=DKD⁻¹ with diagonal unit entries in D, both this integral and the determinant are unchanged.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicit Countable Choice hypothesis inherited by the Hilbert, Fock and surface-measure constructions.
Finiteness of multiplier quadratic expectations and sectorwise and truncation-error bounds in the weak-convergence proof; the inequality is unaffected by reversing the pairing convention.
Convergence of exponential vectors, their pairings and the real exponential estimates used to prove weak convergence.
The power-series definition used in coherent-vector normalization and overlap calculations.
Combining coherent normalization factors and identifying real exponential values.
The modulus identity giving absolute coherent overlap exp(−||u−v||²/2).
The exact radial integral ∫ε^κ dr/r=log(κ/ε) and the positive dyadic-shell norm.
The chart definition and Gram density for angular integration, including the explicit sphere charts in the examples.
Identification of chart angular measure with polar measure, its finiteness and orthogonal invariance.
The radial-angular decomposition of the coherent family's nonnegative norm and energy integrals under Countable Choice.
Null chart seams and poles in the angular example.

seams_checked.note: Compared the actual gauge-data and transverse-space definitions with their uses in the formal-ring and photon-multiplier chains. The phase sign, signature, second-variable-linear pairing, d³k measure, transverse range and Countable Choice hypothesis agree. Graph phases remain independent of spacetime gauge functions; draft supplier status remains explicit.

The formal-coefficient postulate and formal Ward theorem retain invertible K0, coefficient covariance, coefficientwise differentiation, the explicit on-shell current hypotheses and finite longitudinal coefficients. Their conclusions remain finite/formal or tree-level and do not claim convergence or loop identities. Determinant invariance is separately justified.

The massive-tree-annihilation theorem quotes the actual finite/formal matrix-Ward interface with its hypotheses. It explicitly avoids attributing tree-current clauses to that lemma and derives its own current cancellations, including the massless cases, from its spinor supplier.

The soft-current theorem accurately quotes the coherent-tail statement and matches ε=λ/(ℏc), κ=Λ/(ℏc), and C_b=C after its unitary conversion. It handles C=0 separately, uses the infrared conclusions only for C>0, and proves its stronger projective-ray obstruction locally.
